$comment: REALITY Year 2 tokens · rev 19.08.26. Generated from reality-ds.css. Values marked corrected were changed by accessibility audit or measurement after the app shipped — a codebase carrying the old values is pre-audit, not authoritative. Weekday hues and the ink partner map live in day-colours.json (canvas/PDF renderers import that directly).

color.$comment: Palette locked. Majors carry MEANING (named UI jobs); minors carry MOOD (day-code + artwork). No minor takes a UI job — the accent is the one exemption.

accent.$comment: Theme-aware (18.08.26). The second ink is the lead's partner from day-colours.json — the partner map is CANON (19.08.26). Never share a family with the surface. The neverPair list is ADVISORY: warn, do not block.

surface-2.why: collapsed onto bg made every inset, day header, placeholder and skeleton invisible in Day

paper-shade.why: deeper off-paper for poster placeholders before an image paints

fg-faint.why: WCAG AA — .45 measured 3.15:1 and it carries nav labels, hints, placeholders, timestamps

hairline.why: decoration only — never carries text, never the sole indicator

shadow.$comment: Flat down-shift — big offset, almost no blur, no spread. Ink leaking under a lifted edge. Day was corrected upward because the lighter set washed out on cream; Night was already right and the asymmetry is deliberate.

misregister.$comment: Static since 18.08.26 — the drifting 9s/13s loop was retired. Requires isolation:isolate on a background-less ancestor or the negative-z layers vanish silently. Two plates, never three.

space.$comment: 4px ramp, mirroring the 2px borders and 4/8/13 shadow offsets.

type.$comment: Two axes: FAMILY by job (Montserrat names, Grotesk states facts) and CASE by register (.reg-far caps, .reg-near sentence). Register is a closed list, never a distance estimate. Montserrat Alternates is the wordmark only — and the mark is a mixed-font vector, never reproduced from a font-family.

tracking.$comment: Optical ladder, baked per role. One ladder, two offsets: @media print adds .01em, .medium-signage adds .02em and forces weight 700. Never a second table.
tracking.name: 0em
tracking.label: .16em

informational.$comment: Anything you would ACT on — times, rooms, prices, dates, capacities.

decorative.$comment: Labels, eyebrows, tags. Signals, not information.

lineHeight.$comment: Uppercase VI stacks diacritics above cap height; 1.05 clips them.

displayWeight.$comment: Weight 100 loses hairline diacritic strokes at distance.

properNames.$comment: Never uppercased or normalised — .name-block .type-name preserves as given.

diacritics.$comment: Never stripped. Đà Nẵng is never Da Nang on a designed surface.

figures.money: 45.000₫ — dot thousands, currency trailing, no space

snap.job: quick settle — lifts, presses, toggles, theme flip

settle.why: the flip ships at 700ms via html.theme-settling; this token was mislabelled

enter.job: entrances, counters, kinetic type, AND the Day<->Night flip

stagger.job: delay between siblings — cap the total around 6 items

pass.$status: RATIFIED 22.08.26 (G4). Screen timing is canon; the canon card's sets are the print/poster numbers.
pass.$comment: Ink-mark arrival, PRODUCT timing (rev 22.08.26). The parameter sets in guidelines/ink-strip-motion-applied.html are poster-scale — a mark read once at distance. On screen those numbers read as a blip, so the shape is kept and the clock is slowed. Poster/print renderers keep the canon-card numbers; anything on a screen uses these. Scale only, never opacity.

A1.job: full pass — first contact only (splash, hero)

A2.job: quick pass — the default for any in-product surface

A3.job: single plate — short strips and small modules, where cells would smear

A4.job: chained pass — the mark hands the stagger outward to type; outward only, never inward

swap.$comment: Engine B. A cell pulls to 0, re-inks, pops back; unchanged cells never move. Slowed with the pass, same reason.

stagger.$comment: 0 when the swap must land as one event — day tick, section hue

idle.$status: RATIFIED 22.08.26 (G4), as a separate token from motion.pass — the timing and the idle can be taken independently.
idle.$comment: NEW 22.08.26. The press never quite stops: every few seconds one cell lifts and re-prints itself. Default on for any mark without a swap engine. Stops off-screen; a pass or a swap always wins.

every.$comment: jittered so sibling marks never sync into a wave

idle.why: A cell re-inks in its own colour and lands back where it was. Cell order is fixed and every mode already spends its whole palette, so a hue changing on a timer would be SAYING something. The life is in the printing, not the colour.
idle.off: data-idle=off — marks sitting beside a decision (RSVP, void, pay) stay dead still.

thesis: The shadow snaps in on landing.
Press has weight — active goes below rest.

reducedMotion.$comment: Blanket prefers-reduced-motion kills all transitions and animations. Every animated state must be legible at rest; ship the end state in prerendered HTML.

inkMark.$comment: Placement rules for the strip/square that are NOT in ink-strip.json because they are surface-dependent. Full spec: guidelines/ink-strip.html + tokens/ink-strip.json.

openSilhouette.$comment: DECIDED 22.08.26 (G2). The open silhouette is CORRECT on screen and is not to be patched. Canon's 'stock is never on an outer edge or corner' holds for PRINT, where the mark is a solid object on a sheet. On screen, majors / daycode / the short strip terminating on stock is wanted: the corner opening keeps the mark reading as ink laid ON the page rather than a badge sitting on it, and it is what makes cell-switching legible — a cell that pulls to zero at the edge opens the silhouette further instead of punching a hole in a patch. Expect this to matter more as the swap animations are pushed.
openSilhouette.doNotAdd: No ground, no patch, no outline, no keyline. Do not restore the background-comparison test that briefly shipped in ink-motion.js — automatic grounding is gone on purpose.
openSilhouette.optIn: data-ground="on" grounds a single mark on --paper-shade with one module of clear space. For the two cases that need it: a mark over photography, and print export. Never automatic.
openSilhouette.print: Print keeps the canon rule. A print/PDF renderer grounds or insets as needed; the screen does not.
openSilhouette.rejectedAlternative: Re-ordering majors and daycode so they do not terminate on stock. Rejected twice over: reordering is not a parameter, and the termination is now a feature.

decorative.$comment: The mark carries no UI job and no information. It must ship aria-hidden=true, and it must be legible at rest for prefers-reduced-motion. See HANDOFF.md — component contract is an open engineering question.

perSurface.$comment: One mark per surface. The poster exception (hero mark + a QR square) is the only case for two.

qrPairing.$comment: Mark module = QR module x 8.25, which makes a 4x4 square exactly as tall as the code. The code's four-module quiet zone IS stock, so the square butts flush — never a gap, never a rule between them.

choiceHue.$comment: NEW 22.08.26, PENDING RATIFICATION. The first time a MINOR takes a job in the UI, built on the weekday precedent rather than as an exception: the hue IDENTIFIES a choice, it never states a status. Introduced for the quiz quick-fingers round, where four options must be told apart across a dark room in six seconds.
rules: Ink text on every plate, 2px ink border — same as every other coloured fill (the red ACTION exception does not generalise).
Letter, colour and words always travel together. The hue is never the sole carrier of an answer.
No hue ever means right or wrong. Correct is a filled ink plate; incorrect is an ink strike.
Answered / unanswered stays ink — an inset ink ring, never a hue change.
Fixed slot order, like the weekday map. A is always blue.
choiceHue.scope: QUIZ CHOICE SETS ONLY. This is the load-bearing clause, not the hues. It does not license minors anywhere else in the UI and specifically does not license colour-coding event categories, menu sections, room codes or tags — a weekday hue is the only other identifying colour in the system and it stays that way.
choiceHue.why: One screen in the system has a six-second limit and a genuinely dark room. Four near-identical ink plates at arm's length in a loud bar is slower to scan, measurably.
choiceHue.acceptedRisk: Blue and yellow are majors carrying wayfinding and notices. In a choice set they are doing neither. Accepted because the hue is never the sole carrier — letter, colour and words always travel together — and because no hue ever means right or wrong.

focus.$comment: OPEN. Keyboard focus was never designed for the Year 2 system — every prototype relies on the browser default, which is a rounded blue ring and wrong on every count for a zero-radius ink system. Four candidates are rendered in 'Focus States - Options.html'; the pick becomes canon here. Blocking for any web handoff.

decided.$mechanic: TWO IMPRESSIONS OF THE SAME SHAPE, one slipped. The control is two parts: a solid accent PLATE that stays exactly where the button is and never moves, and the FACE (border, fill, label) which slips 4px up-left off that plate. If the whole control translates, nothing has misregistered; it has just moved.

plate.$comment: A SPREAD-LESS BOX-SHADOW, not a negative-z pseudo-element. box-shadow paints behind the element's own background by definition, so the face fill can never be covered and there is no stacking context to get wrong.

face.$comment: Focus is the moment the press slips out of register.

decided.doNotUsePseudoPlate: A ::after plate at z-index:-1 requires isolation:isolate on a BACKGROUND-LESS ancestor. Put isolate on the element carrying the fill and the plate paints ON TOP of that fill — the inverse of the intent. Same trap CLAUDE.md flags for .misreg; it was hit here once.
decided.faceOpaque: The face MUST be opaque. Without its own background the plate shows through it and reads as a fill instead of a second impression.

exceptions.$comment: Three control classes take a 2px ink outline at 3px offset instead of a plate.
exceptions.input: An input is a hole in the paper, not a plate lifted off it.
exceptions.colouredChoicePlate: Already a colour field — an accent plate behind it reads as a second fill.

decided.requires: isolation:isolate on a background-less ancestor, or the negative-z plate vanishes silently.
decided.listSpacing: Rows need 4px of trailing room so the plate does not overlap the next row.
decided.notReusable: Never used for selected, active, hover or current. Focus only, :focus-visible only.
decided.plateNeverSharesFamilyWithSurface: Day leads blue and the wayfinding band IS blue, so on that band the plate prints blue-on-blue and vanishes. On any coloured field the plate takes the accent's PARTNER from day-colours.json: blue field -> pink, notice yellow -> red, action red -> yellow, day-code field -> ink. Same rule the accent already carries; it simply has to be re-declared per band.

requirements: Visible in Day and Night without a second token set.
Never the sole indicator of anything else (not reusable as selected/active).
Works on an ink border, a coloured fill, and a bare text link.
No layout shift — focus must not reflow a row.
:focus-visible only. A mouse press never draws it.

substrate.$comment: Screen values are cream-paper simulations. Press is different by design, not by drift.

printShadowExempt.why: white stock has more headroom and K prints heavier than it looks

openCalls.$comment: All four closed 19.08.26. Recorded so an implementer knows the AA exception is deliberate.

F1-surface-ladder.effect: no change — --surface-2 and --paper-shade stand as shipped

F2-action-label.$comment: Deliberate exception, taken with the measurement in hand: red reads as a filled ink button at distance. Red is the ONLY coloured fill not carrying ink — info, notice and every day-code fill still take ink per --on-day. Do not 'fix' this silently; do not generalise the exception to other fills.

F4-tracking.effect: the six-number optical ladder is canon; no size-derived formula

openCalls.$openedAfter: Four opened 22.08.26 by the website/app layout pass. ALL FOUR CLOSED 22.08.26.

G1-focus.decided: candidate C, misregister plate, with the independent-plate correction and three ink-outline exceptions

G2-open-silhouette.decided: NEITHER. No ground patch and no re-order — the open silhouette is correct on screen and is a feature of cell-switching. Automatic grounding removed.

G4-product-motion.decided: ratified — slowed screen timing AND idle life

dna: 2px ink borders, zero radius — borders carry structure, never tints.
Flat down-shadow — a riso shift, not a soft ambient glow.
Hover lifts, click presses below rest.
Misregister — two offset accent plates behind a hero block, static.
